It's already past midnight.
If you go over that mountain, you can see the sea.
If your score goes over 80 points, you pass.
The ball went over the wall and fell into the neighbor's yard.

explain_en: 넘다 means to pass over a high place or a set number. Don't mix it up with 넘어지다 (to fall down).

examples.en: If it rains, let's meet at a café.
If I'm late, go on in without me.
If you get lost, call me.

examples.ko: 만약 돈이 많으면 뭘 하고 싶어요?
examples.en: If you had a lot of money, what would you want to do?
If you get a fever, go to the hospital.

explain: ‘만약’을 빼도 문장은 돼요. 아직 일어나지 않은 일을 생각해 볼 때 ‘만약’을 쓰면 ‘~면’의 뜻이 더 분명해져요. ‘만일’은 글에서 더 많이 써요.

dict_examples.en: I will surely come to take over, but if I'm late, I hope you'll handle it well.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: You can drop 만약 and the sentence still works. Adding it to something that hasn't happened makes the ‘if’ clearer. 만일 means the same and is more common in writing.

p.n: Almost no difference; 만일 sounds slightly more formal or written.

examples.en: It's been raining nonstop since the morning.
I keep coughing.
My friend kept laughing, so I laughed too.
I want to keep studying Korean.

examples.ko: 전화가 계속 와서 일을 못 했어요.
examples.en: Calls kept coming, so I couldn't work.

explain: 계속은 멈추지 않고 이어진다는 뜻이에요. ‘항상’은 늘 그렇다는 습관이에요. 밤새 비가 오면 ‘계속’, 매일 아침 운동하면 ‘항상’이에요.

explain_en: 계속 means something goes on without stopping. 항상 means ‘always’ as a habit. Rain all night is 계속; exercising every morning is 항상.

en: to come up, to happen; to appear (newly)

examples.en: If anything else comes up, let me know.
A new café opened near my office.

examples.en: I went to a new company and made a lot of friends.
I walked a lot and got a blister on my foot.

examples.en: What happened? You look unwell.

explain: 생기다는 없던 것이 새로 생길 때 써요. ‘어떻게 생겼어요?’는 모양을 묻는 말이에요(What does it look like?).

explain_en: 생기다 is for something that didn't exist coming into being. ‘어떻게 생겼어요?’ asks about appearance (What does it look like?).

examples.en: The conditions for tasty ramyeon are the water and the timing.

examples.ko: 이 집은 조건이 좋아요. 역도 가깝고 싸요.
examples.en: This place meets my conditions. It's close to the station and cheap.

examples.ko: 이 일은 월급은 적지만 조건이 좋아요.
examples.en: The pay for this job is low, but the conditions are good.

examples.ko: 집 조건 중에서 뭐가 제일 중요해요? — 회사에서 가까워야 해요.
examples.en: Of all the conditions for a home, which is most important? — It has to be close to work.

examples.ko: 조건이 하나 있어요. 약속은 꼭 지켜야 해요.
examples.en: I have one condition. You must keep your promise.

explain: ‘조건’은 계약이나 약속의 조건, 집이나 일의 조건을 말해요. 몸이 좋은지 나쁜지는 ‘컨디션’이나 ‘몸 상태’라고 해요.

examples.en: In this case, there's no morning class.
What do you do in a case like this?
That kind of thing happens sometimes.

examples.ko: 버스가 안 오는 경우에는 택시를 타요.
examples.en: If the bus doesn't come, I take a taxi.
If I'm going to be late for work, I send a message.

explain: ‘때’는 시간이고, 경우는 상황이에요. 가끔 있는 일이나 만약의 일을 말할 때 경우를 잘 써요.

explain_en: 때 is about time, while 경우 is about a situation or case. It is a good word for things that happen now and then, or for “in case” situations.

p.n: 사례 means a specific example, not a condition, so it cannot be swapped in.

examples.en: When the water boils, add the ramyeon.
The kettle's boiling. Turn off the stove.
When the soup boils, I turn the heat down.

examples.ko: 물이 안 끓어요. 불이 너무 약해요.
examples.en: The water isn't boiling. The heat is too low.
The milk boiled over.

explain: 끓다는 물이나 국이 스스로 끓는 거예요: 물이 끓어요. 사람이 끓이면 ‘끓이다’를 써요: 물을 끓여요.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: The tea soon began to boil and a rich fragrance spread.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 끓다 is for the liquid itself boiling: 물이 끓어요. When a person boils something, use 끓이다: 물을 끓여요.

dis.h: liquid bubbles by itself, no object

p.n: 끓이다 needs someone doing it, so the subject becomes a person.
